# Braid Keyboard

> Braid Keyboard is a free swipe keyboard for Android that reads two thumbs at once. It works in English and Spanish at the same time and has no internet permission.

Braid Keyboard lets you swipe a word with both thumbs at once, with one thumb, by tapping, or by mixing these in the same word. English and Spanish are built in and work together with no language switch. A free beta language pack adds Portuguese (Brazil), French, German and Italian. It learns the words you type and keeps them on the phone: the app has no internet permission, no account and no ads. It also has slide-to-delete, cursor moves on the space bar, a clipboard with saved texts, 15 themes, 14 key-press effects and typing stats. The app is 5.1 MB.

More languages (beta): Braid Keyboard 1.20.0 can add languages from a pack file. The pack is braid-languages-1.braidpack (about 2.8 MB), a separate download, so the app stays about 5 MB. It holds Portuguese (Brazil), French, German and Italian. These languages are new and tuned only on test swipes so far; feedback is welcome. To add it: download the file on the phone, then in Braid open Settings > Languages > Add languages from a file and pick it, then add a language under Add a language. French gets AZERTY, German QWERTZ, Portuguese and Italian QWERTY, each with its accents on hold. Each language has a word list (about 60,000 words), next-word suggestions, chat slang and swear words handled as in English and Spanish. A keyboard mixes up to two languages. The pack needs Braid 1.20.0 or newer. The app still has no internet permission: the browser downloads the file and Braid only reads it. The file is signed and Braid refuses a file that is not a Braid pack.

How to get it: download braid.apk from the page below on an Android phone and install it. Braid Keyboard is free, with no paid version. It is not on the Play Store and there is no iPhone version. It is built on FlorisBoard (Apache 2.0) by Eddie Bello, in Colombia. Find him at https://strategyandstack.com/, https://www.linkedin.com/in/eddiebello/ and https://www.instagram.com/eddie85u/.

Measured results, with their limits: 96% of real two-thumb swipes were right on the first guess (367 of 381, on the tester's own phone, November 2026). Against Gboard 15.1, on 740 computer-generated one-thumb English swipes on an Android emulator, Braid Keyboard was right on the first guess 98% vs 95% (neat swipes) and 93% vs 91% (sloppy swipes). Its engine was tuned on swipes like these, so read that as on par or slightly ahead, not a clear win.

Other two-thumb keyboards: Keymonk and Nintype (Keyboard 69 on Android) are no longer on Google Play (checked 15 November 2026). Kinetica is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) two-thumb keyboard on F-Droid. Braid Keyboard is its own app with no tie to any of them. It is built on FlorisBoard and is not open source itself.

- [Download the latest braid.apk](https://github.com/eddie85u/braidkeyboard/releases/latest/download/braid.apk): the Android install file
- [Download the language pack (beta)](https://github.com/eddie85u/braidkeyboard/releases/latest/download/braid-languages-1.braidpack): Portuguese, French, German and Italian, for Braid 1.20.0 or newer
- [All versions and release notes](https://github.com/eddie85u/braidkeyboard/releases): every published build
- [Report a bug or ask for something](https://github.com/eddie85u/braidkeyboard/issues): the public issue list
